text.p: These are the leading stories in the Malawi press on Thursday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Expatriates have complained their children receive poor quality education in Malawi due to government bureaucracy and its reluctance to issue temporary employment permits to foreign teachers, Employers Association of Malawi Executive Secretary Wilford Dambuleni said.

- Opposition Alliance for Democracy (AFORD) chairman for northern Malawi Nelson Mwambungu has resigned, taking party colleagues by surprise, but others say he was upset by criticisms levelled at him by party president Chakufwa Chihana.
- The Malawi Savings Bank (MSB) became the third financial institution in Malawi to suffer massive fraud this year after it lost Kwacha 17 million ($1.13 million).

- The inquest into the death of army General Manken Chigawa resumed in Zomba with the legal state advocate asking the court to use tapes recorded at a press conference addressed by Information and Broadcasting Minister Brown Minganjira in 1995.
